newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's UES nine-month profit rises.
newsitem.headline: Russia's UES nine-month profit rises.

text.p: Russian national power company Unified Energy System said on Monday its pre-tax profit on deliveries in the first nine months of this year rose to 659.72 billion roubles from 370.70 billion a year earlier.
However, reflecting Russia's deep payments crisis, UES said its profit on paid-for production rose to 303.99 billion from 248.82 billion.
The company said only 11.7 percent of debts owed to UES were paid in cash, with 82.7 percent paid in some other way.
Percentage of production sold 64.8 pct 80.1 pct
The company said capital investment in the nine months was 4.69 trillion roubles but gave no comparison.
UES (RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii) said its average tariff in the first nine months of this year rose to 205 roubles per kilowatt hour from 155 roubles.

These figures are not prepared to international accounting standards but to Russian accounting standards, which differ significantly from those normally supplied in the West. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
